ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 16661, as amended), articles 4 and 5-2; Commercial Act (Act No. 17255, as amended) articles 543, 549 and 587; Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 17018, as amended); Harbor Act (Act No. 19035, as amended); Enforcement Decree of the Harbor Act; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit beneficial-ownership reporting rules implementing FATF Recommendations 24 and 25; Real Name Financial Transactions Act (Act No. 16221, as amended).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Corporate Existence) of the beneficial owner or corporate sponsor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registrar of the source jurisdiction (for a Korean entity: the District Court Registration Office where the company is registered; for a foreign entity: the equivalent home-country companies registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Source-country notarization, if required; then either (A) if the source jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state, obtain an apostille from its designated competent authority; or (B) if it is not an Apostille Convention state, have the document legalized by the source-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then by the Consular Division of the Embassy/Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that jurisdiction. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and current constitutional documents of each ultimate beneficial owner or sponsor entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the jurisdiction in which each sponsor or UBO entity is incorporated (for Korea: the competent District Court Registration Office; for foreign entities: the applicable national or sub-national companies registrar)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the issuing jurisdiction, if required; then either (A) apostille by the issuing jurisdiction's competent authority when it is a Hague Apostille Convention state; or (B) legalization by the issuing jurisdiction's Ministry of Foreign Affairs followed by legalization by the Consular Division of the Embassy/Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that jurisdiction when the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention state. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative, non-combinable paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing incorporation of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa and Power of Attorney appointing the initial directors and counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the ultimate parent, corporate sponsor, or each member of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified by the corporate secretary and notarized in the source jurisdiction as required; if the source state is an Apostille Convention state, append the source state's apostille; if the source state is not an Apostille Convention state, source-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization followed by Republic of Korea consular legalization. Apostille and consular chains are mutually exclusive and must never be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (draft) of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa containing statutory particulars under the Commercial Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding members and Korean legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For domestic Korean filing, no apostille or consular legalization is required. For use in a country that is an Apostille Convention state, the document must be notarized by a Korean notary and then authenticated by an apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For use in a non-Apostille country, the Korean notarized document must be legalized by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then by the destination country's consulate in Korea. These routes are parallel and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the sponsor, ultimate beneficial owner, or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank maintaining the sponsor or UBO corporate account, subject to a recognized financial supervisor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued on bank letterhead with the bank officer's signature notarized in the bank's home jurisdiction; then either (A) apostille by the bank's home jurisdiction competent authority if it is an Apostille Convention state; or (B) bank's home-jurisdiction Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization followed by Republic of Korea consular legalization if the bank's home jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention state. Apostille and consular legalization are separate paths and may not be combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening covers all founding members, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories, vessel charterers, counterparties, and beneficial owners of counterparties. Use at least three global databases: OFAC SDN and Consolidated Non-SDN Lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List and its subsidiary sanctions lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Korean FIU public warnings under the Financial Transaction Reports Act. Run PEP search using World-Check or equivalent global risk database, negative news, sanctions country watches, and corruption indices. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by any name match, funding from a non-cooperative jurisdiction, refusal of a UBO to disclose, or any vessel-to-vessel bulk-cargo transfer. Every screening result must be time-stamped with the list version, algorithm version, and decision memorandum signed by the AML compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (I-Register) for company-name clearance; Hometax for business registration; KOTRA/Invest Korea One-Stop Service for foreign-investment preliminary confirmation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in Hangul script and must contain the statutory suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' for an LLC. If the desired marketing name is a foreign word, the official registered name must be a phonetically equivalent Hangul transliteration; the English name is only an alias unless separately captured in the articles as a trade name. Korean registry practice applies a four-tier naming review: (i) distinctive token or descriptor, (ii) geographic or industry insertion, (iii) business-purpose words, and (iv) legal-form suffix. Prohibited or sensitive tokens in any tier trigger ministerial pre-approval before clearance.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No automatic extension is granted after the 30-day reservation window; the name is released and a new reservation may be filed. If the registry rejects a name, the applicant receives a written rejection reason. The applicant may file a written objection with the district court registration officer within 14 days, attaching a comparable-name search report and a similarity assessment memorandum. If the rejection is sustained, an administrative appeal may be filed with the competent administrative court within 90 days. In parallel, the fastest remedy is to amend the name by adding a distinctive token and refiling through I-Register. If rejection arises from a sensitive token, obtain the relevant prior approval from the Financial Services Commission, Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Korean Intellectual Property Office, or Ministry of the Interior and Safety and resubmit with that approval letter.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox will be rejected by Korean tax authorities and domestic banks for this stevedoring business because a port cargo-handling license under the Harbor Act requires a physical operating base at or near the port, harbor facilities, equipment, and personnel. A serviced office inside a port business center or a dedicated suite in a permitted harbor commercial building is acceptable if the company has exclusive use, posts signage with its registered name, maintains original books and records there, and has an employee present during business hours. Remote-only domicile arrangements without local commercial substance are not compliant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk is high for this industry; unannounced on-site inspections by the port authority, municipal tax office, Korea Customs Service, labor inspectorate, and immigration office are expected with a likelihood of 55-70% during the first 12 months, rising to about 80% while the stevedoring license application is pending. Preparedness checklist: registered name signboard at reception; valid lease or terminal sublease executed with the port authority; employment contracts and payroll records; resident registration records of on-site staff; original stevedoring equipment and safety insurance policies; hazardous cargo handling manuals; vessel stowage and terminal operating system records; tax invoices; financial ledgers accessible from the registered office; corporate seal and minute book at the registered office; daily crew and contractor access logs.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official government fee; bank service fee, if any, is charged separately by the designated foreign exchange bank

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translation firm and Korean notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per page for Korean-English legal translation with notarization

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, enacted 1962, as amended), Articles 287-2 through 287-74 (Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company), Article 34 (legal registration), Article 317 (establishment registration), together with the Commercial Registration Act (Act No. 4796, as amended); for foreign equity investment, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the President decrees thereunder
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the Local District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Busan District Court Registration Bureau), administered under the Supreme Court of Korea; business and tax registration is administered by the Local District Tax Office under the National Tax Service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration (Commercial Registration Application) under the Commercial Registration Act, with the notarized Articles of Incorporation annexed as the constitutive filing instrument
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. The capital amount specified in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully paid into a Korean bank settlement or escrow account and evidenced by a bank certificate before the court registration application is filed. There is no official blocked-escrow account rule for ordinary stevedoring companies; however, a foreign investor must report inbound equity investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and maintain evidence of receipt. The ad valorem registration tax is calculated at 0.4 percent of subscribed capital plus a 20 percent education surcharge, so with zero subscribed capital the statutory fee component is zero; fixed court, notary, and seal certification charges still apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHANGHOESA (KOREA YUHANGHOESA LLC): WRITTEN UNANIMOUS RESOLUTION ADOPTED IN LIEU OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS MEETING. The undersigned, being the sole member and quota-holder of YUHANGHOESA, a Yuhan Hoesa to be incorporated under the laws of the Republic of Korea, acting by written unanimous consent pursuant to the Articles of Incorporation and Articles 287-2 et seq. of the Korean Commercial Act, and in lieu of an actual meeting of the board of directors, hereby adopts and records the following resolutions, effective as of the date of execution and operative upon completion of commercial registration: (1) Subscription and Capital. The Company confirms that the initial capital contributions set forth in Schedule A were subscribed in full by the members and were paid in cash into the Company's bank settlement account established at the deposit bank, and that the bank certificate of contribution will be filed with the registration application. Upon registration of incorporation, each quota is validly issued, fully paid, and non-assessable. (2) Banking Authorization. The deposit bank is appointed as the Company's principal depository and settlement bank and is irrevocably authorized to open, maintain, and service current accounts in the name of the Company. The Representative Director, jointly with the Chief Financial Officer, is granted signing authority, with a two-signature rule for any payment or transfer exceeding KRW 100,000,000. The corporate seal and specimen signature cards shall be lodged with the bank, and the bank is authorized to honor instructions on that basis. (3) Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is adopted at the address identified in Schedule A, including the port terminal location, within the territorial jurisdiction of the competent District Court. The Representative Director is directed to file the commercial registration application, post the statutory signboard, and maintain the registered office for service of process. (4) Statutory Officers and Delegation. The Company appoints the individuals named in Schedule B as Representative Director, Audit Officer, and Compliance and Safety Officer, each to hold office until the first annual meeting of members or until successors are duly appointed. The Representative Director, jointly with the Compliance and Safety Officer, is authorized to prepare, execute, seal, submit, and receive all filings, licenses, permits, declarations, and consultations necessary for the cargo handling and stevedoring business, including the Harbor Transportation Business Act license, environmental permits, Civil Defense fire clearance, and occupational safety filings. This resolution is effective upon adoption and may be relied upon by all governmental authorities, banks, and third parties dealing with the Company. Adopted this day by unanimous written consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Notarized Articles of Incorporation, and Corporate Seal Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Registry Information Center (internet registration office) and a local Korean Notary Public office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name conflict search on the Supreme Court Registry Information System and the Korean Intellectual Property Office trademark database to ensure that no identical trade name exists in the same court registration district. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language specifying the corporate name, business purpose clauses covering ISIC 5224 cargo stevedoring and bulk port terminal services, registered office address, capital contribution schedule, member identities, director provisions, fiscal year, and dissolution rules. Arrange notarization before a licensed Korean notary public and prepare the corporate seal with a seal certificate. When an offshore entity is a member, execute a power of attorney and apostilled corporate authorization for the Korean incorporator. The proposed office lease must be secured before commercial registration so that the registered office address can be stated precisely.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Passports or ID copies of all incorporators and directors
Board or member resolution of each foreign corporate member
Apostille certificate for foreign corporate authorization documents
Power of attorney appointing the Korean representative
Lease agreement or title evidence for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search reveals a conflicting registered entity or trademark, resubmit with a distinct Korean-language trade name or obtain a coexistence letter from the prior rights holder; if the notary raises formal deficiencies, re-execute the Articles and append a corrected notarial certificate before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution Deposit and Foreign Investment Reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed Korean commercial bank acting as settlement and escrow depository; KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank for foreign investment declaration under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional capital subscription account in the name of the future company at the chosen Korean bank and deposit all subscribed contributions. For a non-resident investor, file the foreign investment report with KOTRA or the head office of a designated foreign exchange bank before remittance, obtain the foreign investment report certificate, and remit the funds through the Korean won settlement account. After receipt of cleared funds, obtain a bank certificate of contribution evidencing the account, subscriber, amount, and payment date. This certificate is a mandatory attachment to the commercial registration filing. No statutory minimum capital applies, but every subscribed amount must be actually credited before the registration application is submitted.
required_dossiers: Provisional subscription account application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Foreign investment report certificate (if any foreign member)
Wire transfer and exchange bank settlement records
Bank certificate of capital contribution
AML/KYC forms for members and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign investment report is returned or corrected, amend the business purpose classification and resubmit through the same foreign exchange bank; if the bank contribution certificate is delayed, obtain a branch-manager confirmation letter and attach it to the registration submission for judicial acceptance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration of Incorporation with the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Busan District Court Registration Bureau)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed Application for Company Registration to the court registration office, attaching the notarized Articles, bank certificate of contribution, consents and identification of directors and officers, certificate of registered seal of the Representative Director, proof of the registered office through lease or title documents, and any powers of attorney. Pay the registration license tax at 0.4 percent of subscribed capital plus a 20 percent education surcharge and the fixed court registration fee. The registration clerk examines the filing; if complete, the court enters the company in the commercial register and issues a certified transcript and registration number. The Yuhan Hoesa obtains legal existence on the date and time of this court registration.
required_dossiers: Application for Commercial Registration (Company Registration)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of capital contribution
Consent forms and passports or resident certificates of directors and officers
Certificate of registered seal of Representative Director
Lease contract and certified copy of building register for registered office
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a supplementation order is issued, cure within fourteen days by filing the omitted or corrected document; if registration is rejected for incorrect jurisdiction, refile at the proper District Court or move the registered office; an administrative appeal or judicial remedy may be pursued against a final refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Corporate Tax Identification with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office under the National Tax Service, through the HomeTax online portal or in-person corporate registration counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the corporate business registration application within twenty days after incorporation with the local tax office governing the registered office. Submit the certified transcript of commercial registration, Articles of Incorporation, registered office lease, and identification of the Representative Director. The tax office will issue the business registration certificate containing the corporate registration number and VAT identification number. In parallel, register for wage withholding, payroll tax, local taxes, and corporate income tax obligations. If the company is foreign-invested, attach the foreign investment report certificate so that the tax office may recognize the foreign-invested enterprise status and any applicable tax treaty benefits.
required_dossiers: Business registration application form
Certified transcript of incorporation registration
Certified copy of Articles of Incorporation
Registered office lease contract
Representative Director identification and seal certificate
Foreign investment report certificate (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office returns the application, correct the registered office or representative details and resubmit online; if processing exceeds twenty days, file a written complaint with the National Tax Service and attach proof of timely submission to avoid late-registration penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cargo Handling and Stevedoring Business License under the Harbor Transportation Business Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Port Logistics Division, Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries; application and inspection through the Regional Office of Oceans and Fisheries (e.g., Busan Regional Office of Oceans and Fisheries)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for cargo handling business approval to the regional maritime authority having jurisdiction over the terminal. Provide evidence of lawful use of berths and storage yards, availability of loading and unloading equipment, arrangement of stevedoring labor, financial capacity, safety and emergency response plans, and liability insurance. The maritime authority will conduct an on-site inspection of the terminal, including gantry cranes, conveyors, dust controls, lighting, weights, and dock safety. Upon approval, the authority issues the cargo handling business registration certificate permitting bulk stevedoring operations for the specified cargo categories. Any later expansion of cargo type or berth requires prior amendment approval.
required_dossiers: Cargo handling business application form
Certificate of business registration
Articles of Incorporation and board resolution
Terminal lease or port authority operating concession
Equipment title, lease, or rental contracts
Safety and emergency response plan
Liability and industrial accident insurance certificates
Financial capability statement and bank reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the maritime authority issues a supplementation notice, submit the requested documents within fifteen days; if the site inspection discloses deficiencies, install or repair the required dust, fire, or load-control equipment and request re-inspection; a license denial may be appealed to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries and subsequently reviewed by the administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Registration, Civil Defense Fire Permit, and Occupational Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Environment through the regional Environmental Management Office; local Fire Department under the National Fire Agency; Ministry of Employment and Labor and Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct the environmental screening or registration for the terminal operation with the regional environmental office, including the Clean Air Conservation Act permit for dust-generating facilities and Waste Control Act registration for cargo residues and wastes. Submit an application to the local Fire Department for fire and Civil Defense approval covering warehouses, offices, and cargo handling structures, then obtain the completion inspection after installation of fire detection, hydrants, extinguishers, and evacuation systems. File a workplace safety plan with the Ministry of Employment and Labor under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and obtain KOSHA review if bulk cargo includes hazardous chemicals. Commission structural load inspections for cranes, gantries, and conveyor supports and maintain the reports for Civil Defense inspections.
required_dossiers: Environmental impact assessment or screening forms and exemption letter
Air pollutant emission forms and dust management plan
Waste registration and hazardous waste manifest framework
Fire safety construction approval and completion inspection forms
Building plans showing firefighting systems and evacuation routes
Occupational safety plan and KOSHA review report
Structural load inspection report for terminal equipment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the environmental office or Fire Department issues a correction order, implement the required technical control, complete the supplemental inspection, and resubmit; if KOSHA identifies a major accident hazard, revise the process safety management plan within the ordered period; any rejection may be challenged by administrative appeal and injunctive relief before the competent administrative court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF), Port Logistics Division, together with the Regional Office of Oceans and Fisheries for the terminal location; municipal and local Fire Department for physical premises clearance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Cargo Handling Business Registration and Operating License under the Harbor Transportation Business Act, covering stevedoring, loading, unloading, and dock-side transfer of bulk cargo

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Environmental Impact Assessment Division, supported by the regional Environmental Management Office and Korea Environment Corporation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Existing terminal stevedoring operation: exempt from a Full Environmental Impact Assessment but subject to Smaller-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment, environmental registration, and pollution facility permitting; greenfield terminal construction or a major expansion beyond statutory thresholds requires a Full Environmental Impact Assessment under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The terminal must comply with Korean Clean Air Conservation Act and Water Environment Conservation Act standards. Typical operational limits are: facility boundary PM10 no greater than 100 ug/m3 and PM2.5 no greater than 50 ug/m3 on a 24-hour average; treated washdown wastewater discharged only after achieving BOD no greater than 10 mg/L, COD-Mn no greater than 40 mg/L, suspended solids no greater than 40 mg/L, total nitrogen no greater than 30 mg/L, and total phosphorus no greater than 4 mg/L; if liquid bulk or chemical cargo is handled, vapor recovery and closed loading systems must achieve at least 95 percent recovery efficiency; hazardous waste residues must be segregated, manifested, stored for no more than six months without approval, and transported to a licensed waste treatment facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety and Civil Defense Permit from the local Fire Department, including fire detection, hydrant network, extinguishers, and evacuation plan approval, followed by a final completion inspection; structural load inspection certificates for cranes, gantries, hoppers, and conveyor supports; occupational safety and health clearance from the Ministry of Employment and Labor, with KOSHA technical review for hazardous bulk materials; and mandatory subscription to industrial accident compensation insurance plus port terminal liability coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign non-resident entities must register with the National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax portal or a local tax office to obtain a Business Registration Number (BRN). Required documents include: certificate of incorporation, certificate of foreign registration, passport of the legal representative, and a domestic place of business or a tax representative appointment if no permanent establishment exists. The application is submitted online or in person; the BRN is issued within 3-5 business days and serves as the VAT registration number.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration for all taxable supplies; simplified taxation for small businesses with annual revenue below KRW 80 million (services) or KRW 48 million (goods)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing via the HomeTax system; all tax invoices must be issued electronically and transmitted to the NTS within 1 day after issuance. No real-time clearance but electronic submission is required. Anti-fraud measures include digital signature and validation of invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated. Services provided to non-residents and used outside Korea are zero-rated if they meet the criteria under the VAT Act, including stevedoring services for international shipping. The service must be supplied to a non-resident and the benefit must be received outside Korea.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is claimed without proper documentation or if foreign exchange is not received within 180 days, the zero-rating is reversed and VAT becomes due. Penalties include additional tax of 40% of the unpaid VAT, plus interest, and potential criminal penalties for fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea operates a liberalized foreign exchange system underpinned by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and regulations promulgated by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, with the Bank of Korea serving as the central bank and enforcing reporting requirements through designated foreign exchange banks. The won is fully convertible on current account transactions, including trade-related payments, service fees, dividends, and loan interest, subject to submission of supporting documents and foreign exchange purpose codes. Capital account transactions are generally convertible but require prior declaration or reporting to the Bank of Korea or a designated foreign exchange bank; inbound foreign direct investment is reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Export proceeds are not subject to mandatory conversion or surrender to the central bank; however, exporters must receive payment within a statutory period and report settlement evidence. Profit remittance by a foreign-invested company is permissible once audited financial statements and tax clearance are provided, but requires bank confirmation of the foreign investment report and proof of dividend source. Temporary restrictions may be invoked in balance-of-payments emergencies, but current practice imposes no material convertibility hurdles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, an exporter of goods must collect the full export proceeds within 18 months from the date of export clearance, unless a temporary permit for extension is granted by the Minister of Economy and Finance through a designated foreign exchange bank. There is no mandatory conversion or surrender ratio: the statutory surrender requirement was abolished in 1999. Exporters may maintain foreign currency receipts in domestic foreign-currency deposit accounts, convert to KRW at a bank rate, or use them for approved overseas purposes; however, the receipt itself must be reported and settled through a designated foreign exchange bank so that the Bank of Korea can monitor balance-of-payments flows. Failure to meet the collection deadline triggers customs export license rectification, a fine under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and adverse KYC impact.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment Purchase Price Deposit)
Trade Disbursement and Stevedoring Collections Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Foreign digital EMI and neobank service providers are not authorized to open won-denominated current accounts, process trade settlements, or provide corporate treasury rails for Korean-resident entities unless they separately hold a license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and are registered as a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. No major offshore Tier-1 EMI currently satisfies this dual licensing requirement; therefore, fintech EMI viability is Low and legally constrained. The port stevedoring LLC must rely on domestic Tier-1 commercial banks for escrow, settlement, FX conversion, and trade clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and the Financial Action Task Force-aligned AML guidelines, statutory directors or authorized signatories must generally appear in person at a Korean bank branch for corporate account opening and beneficial owner verification. Remote consular proxy opening is not broadly permitted for resident Korean corporations; however, for non-resident foreign directors, some banks accept a notarized power of attorney executed before the Korean consulate plus a live video interview, provided at least one local representative or compliance officer attends the branch interview. Physical branch attendance remains mandatory for the initial KYC interview, straight-through processing is not allowed for the port terminal entity without a full in-person risk assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner opacity: the Korean LLC ledger or shareholder register reveals bearer-like or nominee shareholder arrangements, delaying identification of any natural person holding 25% or greater ownership or control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry of the Korean LLC; certified register of shareholders or LLC member ledger; signed UBO declaration under the Financial Transaction Reports Act; notarized IDs and passports of all natural persons in the ownership chain; detailed group ownership chart; corroborating signed financial statements and an external accountant confirmation that no undisclosed trust, nominee, or bearer arrangement exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds insufficiency for the inbound equity injection: remittance originates from a third country unrelated to the Korean entity's ownership chain, or from an entity with no operating history and possible crypto-linked or high-velocity deposits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month original bank statements of the remitter; share subscription agreement or investment contract; corporate resolution approving the capital injection; independent appraisals supporting the valuation of bulk port terminal assets; source-of-wealth affidavit with a documentary trail covering dividend pass-through, real estate sale deeds, or a registered loan agreement; and the purpose-specific foreign exchange report filed with the designated bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering artifact in stevedoring operations: service invoices for cargo handling, shore crane rental, railcar loading, or wharfage are inflated or do not match vessel manifests, port authority tariffs, and terminal gate records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid ISIC 5224 stevedoring license; port authority terminal concession agreement; corresponding bills of lading and cargo manifests; tariff and demurrage schedule filed with the port authority; independent tally company reports; vessel arrival and departure logs; scale house and tally receipts; and an invoice-level reconciliation worksheet matching volumes, vessel calls, and handling rates across the most recent 12 months of trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic sanctions and maritime counterparty exposure: target vessel, charterer, cargo owner, or beneficiary appears on UN, EU, OFAC, FSS, or Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions lists, involving North Korea, Russia, or designated bulk-commodity trade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Time-stamped sanctions screening records for all vessels including IMO numbers; vessel ownership and beneficial ownership chart; charter party contracts; cargo origin and ultimate consignee documentation; freight payment instructions; port state control clearance; denial list and PEP database outputs with exact audit trails; and a legal opinion confirming that the cargo and vessel chain do not breach UN Security Council resolutions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the foreign capital as a serial SWIFT MT103 or MT202 payment to the capital escrow account at the designated foreign exchange bank in Korea, using the inbound remittance purpose code corresponding to foreign direct investment through acquisition of equity in a domestic corporation. Before remittance, file the foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act with KOTRA or the designated bank; the bank then opens an escrowed purchase-price deposit account and issues a certificate of deposit. After shares are issued, the bank reports receipt to the Bank of Korea and provides the foreign investment registration certificate. For capital verification of the port terminal LLC, the external auditor issues a capital verification letter based on the escrow account balance statement, inward remittance evidence, the share issuance resolution, and the foreign investment report certificate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of bulk cargo stevedoring fees, pier and wharfage charges, vessel hire, and terminal equipment costs, use domestic KRW clearing through the Bank of Korea wire system and Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute rails for local counterparties. For cross-border counterparties, execute SWIFT MT103 direct remittances for invoices denominated in USD, EUR, JPY, or CNY, and use irrevocable at-sight commercial letters of credit or documentary collections for high-value terminal equipment and bulk-commodity transactions. Port authority clearing gates and customs duty payment systems must be utilized for statutory charges, and every outbound payment must carry a valid foreign exchange purpose code plus retained beneficial owner data.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward exchange contract with a designated foreign exchange bank, supported by a genuine trade-related receivable or payable exposure
Cross-currency swap for long-term foreign currency borrowings with matching debt-service cash flows and underlying FDI registration
Vanilla FX option (put or call) with premium payment based on a documented committed foreign exchange line

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) is generally not accessible to Korean-resident corporates; it is restricted to domestic banks and eligible offshore participants, and therefore is not recommended for the terminal operating company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment (including member list, financial statements, and tax adjustments for the business year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December fiscal-year-end entity, on or before March 31 of the immediately following year; for other fiscal-year-ends, within three months from the fiscal-year-end. A one-month filing extension to April 30 is available on application by the original due date, but the tax payment due date is not extended.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surcharge of 20% of the unpaid tax amount; under-reporting surcharge of 10% for negligent understatement and up to 40% for fraudulent concealment or offshore evasion; statutory overdue interest currently 0.022% per day from the original due date until full settlement; persistent delinquency results in tax seizure, business registration cancellation, and court-ordered dissolution as the Korean administrative strike-off equivalent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surtax on Corporate Income Tax (distributed to the province and municipality where the principal place of business is located)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Government and Local Tax Collection Agency, administratively collected through the National Tax Service filing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory deadline as the corporate income tax return and payment: for a December fiscal-year-end entity, March 31 of the following year; for other fiscal-year-ends, within three months after the fiscal-year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a 20% non-filing surcharge and a 10% under-reporting surcharge; overdue local tax accrues daily delay interest calculated at the statutory local tax rate of 0.022% per day until payment, with local-government asset seizure and business registration strike-off proceedings for chronic non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual External Audit Report and Financial Statements Filing, required only if the mandatory audit threshold is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system, with the audited financial statements maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The statutory auditor must be appointed within four months from the start of each business year; the annual members' meeting must approve the audited financial statements within six months after the fiscal-year-end; for a December fiscal-year-end, approval must occur by June 30 and the audit report must be submitted to the FSS within two weeks after approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or obtain an audit is subject to administrative fines up to KRW 50 million, criminal sanctions under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc., and formal issuance of a corrective order by the FSS; misleading audit-related disclosures may also invalidate the company's tax-filing reliance and expose directors and managers to personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Stevedoring Business Performance Report for the Port Cargo Handling Business Licence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Regional Office of Oceans and Fisheries, Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 31 of each year for the preceding calendar year, or on the anniversary date / calendar date expressly stated as a condition of the stevedoring terminal licence.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-submission attracts administrative fines up to KRW 5 million, suspension of the stevedoring licence for up to three months, and repeated non-compliance may result in revocation of the port cargo handling licence and removal from the approved terminal operator register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Invested Company Annual Report and Foreign Investor Status Confirmation, applicable because non-resident ownership is permitted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA or the relevant Foreign Exchange Processing Bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of each fiscal year; for a December fiscal-year-end entity, on or before March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual foreign investment status report may lead to administrative fines, loss of foreign-invested company registration status, disqualification from foreign investment protection and tax incentives, and an order to make a retroactive foreign exchange reporting correction.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Yuhan Hoesa is legally required to obtain an independent certified CPA audit under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc. where, at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, the company's total assets are at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.0 million at 1,340 KRW/USD). The Act does not separately impose a turnover or headcount threshold for a private port stevedoring LLC; the mandatory quantitative balance-sheet trigger is total assets of KRW 12 billion or more. In addition, a statutory audit is required where the company is a financial service company, designated by the Financial Services Commission as a public-interest company, files consolidated financial statements under K-IFRS, or is a subsidiary of an audited parent that is consolidated into a K-IFRS reporting group. A Yuhan Hoesa with total assets below KRW 12 billion and no public-interest designation is exempt from mandatory independent CPA audit, although members may voluntarily appoint an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is the governing framework for all companies required to undergo external audit; a non-audited private company with total assets below KRW 12 billion may prepare financial statements under K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, including the SME Accounting Standards codified by the Korea Accounting Standards Board). The financial statements must comprise a balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in members' equity, cash flow statement, notes, and directors' certification; for tax computation, book earnings are reconciled to taxable income under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no stand-alone annual beneficial-ownership confirmation return to a central Korean registry. Instead, a Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a current register of members and a list of managers/directors, and any transfer of a membership interest is effective against the company only when recorded in the member register. The company must update the member register promptly and report the ownership change to the National Tax Service through the next corporate income tax return; if a foreign investor acquires or transfers membership interest, a change of foreign investment report must be filed with KOTRA or the applicable foreign exchange processing bank within 30 days from the closing date. For AML and KYC purposes, the company must confirm and update beneficial-ownership identification whenever it engages in covered financial transactions or when the bank or statutory agent requests such information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Yuhan Hoesa member register with quota ownership percentages)
Register of Charges or Security Interests
Minute Book of Members' Resolutions and Managers' Resolutions
Commercial Books and Source Documents retained for 10 years

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - USD 40,000 per year if the mandatory audit threshold is triggered; USD 0 if the LLC remains below the KRW 12 billion asset threshold and no voluntary audit is chosen
